title: Relative flatness is equivalent across elementary module devissage
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$, $s=f(x)$. Let $g:(X',x')\to(X,x)$ and $e:(S',s')\to(S,s)$ be elementary etale neighbourhoods (etale and inducing isomorphisms of residue fields at the marked points), and let $f':X'\to S'$ satisfy $fg=ef'$. Suppose $X',Z',Y',S'$ are affine, $i:Z'\to X'$ is a closed immersion of finite presentation, $\pi:Z'\to Y'$ is finite over $S'$, $h:Y'\to S'$ is smooth of relative dimension $n=\dim_x\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_s)$ with geometrically integral fibres, and $\mathcal G$ is a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{Z'}$-module with $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$. Let $z'\in Z'$ satisfy $i(z')=x'$, put $y'=\pi(z')$, and assume $h(y')=s'$, $\pi^{-1}(y')=\{z'\}$ and $\kappa(y')/\kappa(s')$ purely transcendental. These are precisely the elementary devissage data of [lem-trf-elementary-module-devissage], with module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]; explicitly $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\mathcal F_s$ is the pullback of $\mathcal F$ to $X_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Schemes, affine spectra, quasi-coherence, finite type, dimension, smoothness, etaleness, finite morphisms, closed immersions, finite presentation of morphisms, residue fields, integrality and purely transcendental extensions have the meanings of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension]. The following conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ on some neighbourhood of $x$; $\mathcal G$ is flat over $S'$ on some neighbourhood of $z'$; $\pi_*\mathcal G$ is flat over $S'$ on some neighbourhood of $y'$. Also the following stalkwise conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$; $\mathcal G_{z'}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$; $(\pi_*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S',s'}$. Flatness over a base means flatness of these module stalks, as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. No local finite-presentation assumption on $f$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 057U, lemma-devissage-flat, both neighbourhood and stalkwise assertions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-closed-support-flatness] with $(U,T,Z,a)=(X',S',Z',f')$ and the given $f,g,e,i,\mathcal F,\mathcal G$. Both $g$ and $e$ are etale and $i$ is closed by hypothesis. The square is $fg=ef'$. Inverting the given $\mathcal O_{X'}$-linear isomorphism $i_*\mathcal G\cong g^*\mathcal F$ supplies the helper's specified isomorphism $H=g^*\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal G$. The devissage data give $f'i=h\pi$, so the helper's structure map $ai$ on $\mathcal G$ is exactly $h\pi$. Its marked points are $z',x',x,s'$, since $i(z')=x'$, $g(x')=x$, and $f'(x')=h(\pi(z'))=s'$. Finite-type quasi-coherence supplies the required quasi-coherence of both modules. The helper's neighbourhood equivalence therefore identifies (1) and (2), through flatness of $g^*\mathcal F$ over $S'$ near $x'$.

Apply [lem-trf-finite-pushforward-flatness-singleton] with $(Y,Z)=(Y',Z')$, finite $\pi$, quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$, and marked points $z',y'=\pi(z')$. Since $S'$ is affine, choose a presentation $q:S'\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}A$. Use $qh$ and $qh\pi$ as the helper's structure maps. At every point $v$ of $Y'$ or $Z'$, the isomorphism on base local rings induced by $q$ identifies the two scalar actions on the same module stalk. Relabelling scalars along a ring isomorphism preserves tensor products and injectivity, hence flatness; the underlying open neighbourhoods are unchanged. Thus the helper's relative-flatness assertions over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ give the assertions over $S'$. Its singleton-fibre hypothesis is precisely the assumed $\pi^{-1}(\{y'\})=\{z'\}$. Its neighbourhood equivalence therefore identifies (2) and (3); with Step 1 this proves all three neighbourhood conditions equivalent.

For the separate stalkwise assertion, [lem-trf-etale-closed-support-flatness] with Step 1's substitution identifies (a) with (b). Its scalar actions are through $f$ and $f'i=h\pi$, and its base point is $f'(x')=s'$. The canonical germ isomorphism of [lem-trf-finite-pushforward-flatness-singleton] is linear over $\mathcal O_{S',h(y')}=\mathcal O_{S',s'}$; its stalkwise equivalence identifies (b) with (c). Transitivity gives the required stalkwise equivalence. These applications use neither local finite presentation of $f$ nor any inference from flatness at one stalk to flatness on a neighbourhood.
